content.text:
The build is green. 

I implemented the daily-limit rule following the existing capacity/uniqueness pattern, keeping structural impact minimal — three brand-new small classes (each a single method with no surrounding class complexity) plus one new escalation YAML, and I only edited **one** existing file:

- `RequireDailyCapacity` — counts owners whose `registrationDate` is today; throws `DailyLimitException` at 100+.
- `DailyLimitException` (checked) + `DailyLimitExceptionHandler` — responds **429 Too Many Requests**.
- `...DailyLimitException.yml` — registers the handler.
- `owners.POST.yml` — a new `dailyLimit` step wired after `capacity`, before `build` (so the cap is enforced before an owner is constructed/saved).

I did not touch any existing function class, so no high-WMC method was modified. All tests pass (`BUILD SUCCESS`).
